title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 60 (Publication of Authorised, Subscribed and Paid-Up Capital)

content.overview: Section 60(1) requires that where any notice, advertisement or other official publication, or any business letter, billhead or letter paper of a company contains a statement of the amount of the authorised capital of the company, such notice, advertisement or other official publication, or such letter, billhead or letter paper shall also contain a statement, in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters, of the amount of the capital which has been subscribed and the amount paid-up. Section 60(2) provides that if any default is made in complying with sub-section (1), the company shall be liable to pay a penalty of ten thousand rupees and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to pay a penalty of five thousand rupees, for each default.
content.glance: If authorised capital is stated in notices, ads or stationery, subscribed and paid-up capital must also be stated equally prominently; default attracts fixed penalties (company ₹10,000; officer ₹5,000 per default).
content.study: Where any notice, advertisement or other official publication, or any business letter, billhead or letter paper of a company contains a statement of the amount of the authorised capital of the company, such notice, advertisement or other official publication, or such letter, billhead or letter paper shall also contain a statement, in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters, of the amount of the capital which has been subscribed and the amount paid-up (s. 60(1)). If any default is made in complying with the requirements of sub-section (1), the company shall be liable to pay a penalty of ten thousand rupees and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to pay a penalty of five thousand rupees, for each default (s. 60(2)). Current-law framing: identify whether authorised capital is stated in the listed media; if so, require equally prominent and conspicuous statements of subscribed capital and paid-up capital; apply the fixed penalties in s. 60(2) for each default.

sections.heading: Trigger (s. 60(1))
sections.body: Any notice, advertisement or other official publication, or any business letter, billhead or letter paper that contains a statement of the amount of the authorised capital of the company.

sections.heading: Disclosure requirement (s. 60(1))
sections.body: Such document must also contain a statement, in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters, of the amount of the capital which has been subscribed and the amount paid-up.

sections.heading: Penalty for default (s. 60(2))
sections.body: Company liable to penalty of ten thousand rupees; every officer in default liable to penalty of five thousand rupees, for each default.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Prevents a misleading impression of the company’s capital strength created by stating only authorised capital.

provisions.title: Publication of authorised, subscribed and paid-up capital

examples.title: Compliant stationery
examples.body: Letter paper states authorised capital ₹10 crore, subscribed capital ₹6 crore and paid-up capital ₹5 crore in equally prominent and conspicuous characters. Section 60(1) is complied with.

examples.title: Misleading advertisement
examples.body: An advertisement states only ‘Authorised capital ₹100 crore’ without equally prominent statements of subscribed and paid-up capital. Section 60(1) is breached; s. 60(2) penalties apply for each default.

examples.title: Equal prominence required
examples.body: A notice states authorised capital in large bold type but places subscribed and paid-up figures in small footnote type. The requirement of ‘equally prominent position and equally conspicuous characters’ is not met.

hypotheticals.question: Can a company advertise only its authorised capital?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. If authorised capital is stated in any notice, advertisement, official publication, business letter, billhead or letter paper, s. 60(1) requires that subscribed capital and paid-up capital also be stated in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters.

hypotheticals.question: What is the penalty for default under s. 60?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under s. 60(2), the company is liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees and every officer of the company who is in default is liable to a penalty of five thousand rupees, for each default.

misconceptions.trap: Stating authorised capital alone is always fine.
misconceptions.correction: Section 60(1) requires subscribed and paid-up capital to be stated equally prominently whenever authorised capital is stated in the listed media.

misconceptions.trap: Any mention of capital figures attracts s. 60.
misconceptions.correction: The section is triggered only when a statement of the amount of the authorised capital appears; the duty is then to add equally prominent subscribed and paid-up figures.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 60 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify whether the document is a notice, advertisement, official publication, business letter, billhead or letter paper. II. Check whether it contains a statement of the amount of authorised capital. III. If yes, verify whether subscribed capital and paid-up capital are also stated in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters. IV. If not, record breach of s. 60(1) and apply the penalties in s. 60(2) (company ₹10,000; officer ₹5,000 per default). V. Conclude.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: IRAC-style analysis aligned to the statutory text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions on a Section 60 default contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The document(s) relied on; the statement of authorised capital; absence or unequal prominence of subscribed and paid-up figures; the statutory text of s. 60(1)–(2); the fixed penalties; identification of the company and officers in default; relief sought.

examTips: Trigger: statement of authorised capital in listed media.
Require subscribed + paid-up equally prominent and conspicuous.
